subject: Proposed staged caps + prohibited-testing safeguards (MSA & Order Form)
messages:
From: Aline Dubois <aline.dubois@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form — liability cap and benchmarking exceptions (redline attached)

Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our procurement redline to the MSA and the draft Order Form. Two items that procurement needs clarity on before we can move to legal:

1) Liability cap: our team prefers a standard cap of the greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees. Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept a fixed-dollar cap, or whether you require a multiple-of-fees approach?

2) Benchmarking / prohibited testing: Acme is concerned about "prohibited testing" (attempts to reverse-engineer, benchmark, or systematically probe the model). We need language that: (a) prohibits those tests without prior consent, and (b) preserves remedies if such testing causes data leakage or IP exposure. Specifically, procurement wants clarity whether damages related to prohibited testing are excluded from the liability cap and whether injunctive relief is available.

Attached: ACME_Redline_MSA.docx, ACME_SOC2_Summary.pdf. Can you please propose specific redline language for (a) a staged cap approach (MSA-level vs Order Form-specific cap) and (b) explicit carveouts for damages tied to prohibited testing/benchmarking? Our timeline is tight — procurement hopes to have terms agreed by end of week.

Thanks,
Aline
Head of Procurement — Acme Health
aline.dubois@acmehealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability cap and benchmarking exceptions (redline attached)

Folks — looping you in. Key asks from Acme: fixed cap vs multiple-of-fees, and whether prohibited-testing damages get carved out of the cap. My preference (and what I think we can sell):

- Staged cap model: MSA-level cap = 3x most recent 12 months' fees (or $3M floor), with the ability to set an Order Form-specific cap (e.g., 6 months fees) for a limited pilot/PO period. This lets us protect the platform while giving procurement predictability.
- Carveouts: we should list explicit carveouts from the cap for (i) willful misconduct, (ii) material breach of data security resulting in data exfiltration, and (iii) breaches involving IP/unauthorized model extraction or reverse-engineering via prohibited testing.
- Remedies for prohibited testing: immediate suspension + right to terminate, injunctive relief; we should also state that damages arising from prohibited testing that cause data loss or IP harm are not subject to the cap (uncapped).

Laura — can you draft language that (1) defines "Prohibited Testing" tightly (so it isn't used broadly by customers), and (2) ties the remedy set (injunctive relief / uncapped damages / termination) to that definition? Marissa — if we adopt an Order Form-specific cap, can you prepare a redline Order Form (6 months fees) and a fallback that stays within our typical commercial guardrails? Karthik — flag any commercial risks we should pre-authorize for the AE to offer (credits, time-limited trial, etc.).

Goal: return to Acme with defendable legal language and a small commercial concession by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability cap and benchmarking exceptions (redline attached)

Kim / team — high level thoughts and a draft snippet. I tried to balance enforceability and commercial optics.

- Definition: "Prohibited Testing" — limited to: (a) automated or manual attempts to systematically extract model weights or internal parameters; (b) scripted / repeated probing intended to reconstruct training data or confidential system prompts; (c) use of load/throughput tests that intentionally bypass our rate limits and batching controls in order to measure internal performance characteristics.

- Remedies / carveouts (proposed language snippet):

  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the liability cap set forth in Section [X] shall not apply to (i) damages resulting from Provider's willful misconduct; (ii) damages arising from a material breach of Provider's data security obligations that results in unauthorized access to or exfiltration of Customer Data; and (iii) damages arising from Customer's engagement in Prohibited Testing. For clarity, Customer acknowledges that Provider may seek injunctive relief and temporary or permanent suspension of access for any conduct constituting Prohibited Testing, and may pursue uncapped monetary damages for loss or harm caused by such conduct."

Notes / negotiation points:
- Customers will push back on uncapped language; we should offer commercial compromises (e.g., pre-authorized credits or a limited pilot cap) for smaller customers.
- Precise drafting matters: tie "Prohibited Testing" to concrete actions (example list) to avoid ambiguity.
- Think about detection: if we intend to enforce suspension/injunctive relief, we need operational signals (logs, rate anomaly alerts) and an escalation path documented in the console. Marissa — can you add a short SOP note for the support/ops teams for how to handle suspected Prohibited Testing?

I'll attach a redline snippet. If we get Acme to accept the staged caps + carveouts we can close quickly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability cap and benchmarking exceptions (redline attached)

Thanks — quick commercial note: Acme is price-sensitive. If we insist on uncapped damages for prohibited testing they will almost certainly ask for a higher cap elsewhere or a discount. Two play options we can pre-authorize:

1) Offer a 10% one-time credit on the first year's invoice in exchange for accepting our staged cap + carveouts.
2) Offer a 6-month limited pilot with an Order Form cap at 6 months' fees (no change to MSA cap) and include a very explicit Acceptable Use Schedule that prohibits Prohibited Testing (and retains injunctive relief).

Either option keeps our MSA intact while giving procurement predictability. Happy to lead the AC if legal signs off.

Karthik

Team — I prepared an Order Form redline that implements the 6-month cap for the pilot and added a short Acceptable Use Schedule. Key pieces:

- Order Form, Section 2: Total Liability Cap = the greater of (i) six (6) months of Fees paid under this Order Form, or (ii) $250,000.
- Addendum A (Acceptable Use): defines Prohibited Testing with 6 concrete examples and states that Provider may suspend access pending investigation.
- Remedy paragraph references MSA Section [X] so that all carveouts there (willful misconduct, data exfiltration, Prohibited Testing) remain uncapped.

I attached: OrderForm-6moCap_redlined.docx. Also adding a short DocuSign envelope so we can send Order Form + Acceptable Use addendum for countersignature quickly (link below).

Proposed negotiation script for AE: "We can accept a short-term Order Form cap for the pilot to give you predictability. The MSA still contains the standard cap and carveouts for misuse. If you need a higher MSA-level cap we can route to commercial for review."
